title: `strtolower()`/`strtoupper()` and related functions are no longer locale-sensitive
summary: As of PHP 8.2, `strtolower()`, `strtoupper()`, and a family of related case-conversion and case-insensitive functions no longer consult the current locale; they always perform ASCII-only case conversion as if the locale were "C", so previously locale-dependent behavior on non-ASCII bytes changes silently.
new_code_policy: On a PHP 8.2+ floor, do not write code that expects strtolower()/strtoupper() (or the related functions listed in details) to case-convert non-ASCII bytes based on the process locale; they only ever touch ASCII A-Z/a-z now. When locale- or encoding-aware case folding is genuinely required, call mb_strtolower()/mb_strtoupper() with an explicit, known encoding.
existing_code_policy: Audit call sites that feed non-ASCII input to strtolower(), strtoupper(), or the related functions under the old assumption that a non-"C" locale would case-convert it; on PHP 8.2+ those bytes now pass through unchanged. Do not mechanically replace every call with mb_strtolower()/mb_strtoupper() - first confirm the call site's actual input encoding and whether locale-based conversion was ever the intended behavior, since the multibyte functions require a known encoding and can themselves change output if applied blindly.
guideline: Do not rely on strtolower()/strtoupper() or the related case-conversion/case-insensitive functions being locale-sensitive; they now always perform ASCII-only case conversion regardless of the process locale. Reach for mb_strtolower()/mb_strtoupper() with an explicit encoding when locale- or multibyte-aware case folding is actually needed.
details: Before PHP 8.2, strtolower() and strtoupper() consulted the locale set via setlocale(LC_CTYPE, ...), so under a non-"C" locale they could case-convert non-ASCII bytes (for example accented Latin-1 characters) as a side effect of whatever locale happened to be active process-wide - behavior that was also process-global and easy to get wrong across threads or requests. As of PHP 8.2, both functions always behave as if the locale were "C": they convert only ASCII A-Z/a-z and leave every other byte untouched, no matter the active locale. The same ASCII-only treatment now applies to stristr(), stripos(), strripos(), lcfirst(), ucfirst(), ucwords(), str_ireplace(), array_change_key_case(), and SORT_FLAG_CASE-based sorting, since each relies on the same underlying case-folding primitive. mb_strtolower()/mb_strtoupper() are unaffected by this change and remain the correct tool for locale- or multibyte-aware case conversion. Here introduced_in is set to 8.2 because that is the minor this behavior actually changed in - the field exists so this behavior_change rule can be range-gated on the feature axis, and it is not a claim that PHP 8.2 introduced strtolower()/strtoupper() themselves, which have existed since PHP's earliest versions.
notes: The same ASCII-only case-folding change also applies to stristr(), stripos(), strripos(), lcfirst(), ucfirst(), ucwords(), str_ireplace(), array_change_key_case(), and SORT_FLAG_CASE-based sorting, not only to strtolower()/strtoupper().

No automatic replacement is offered because swapping in mb_strtolower()/mb_strtoupper() is not a safe mechanical substitution: the multibyte functions require a known text encoding and behave differently on multibyte input, so whether a rewrite is correct, and which encoding to pass, depends on the call site's actual data rather than on the function name alone.

This is a silent behavior change, not a deprecation: no warning or notice is raised, so code that depended on locale-based non-ASCII case conversion silently produces different output on an affected PHP 8.2+ runtime, with no diagnostic pointing at the cause.

Evidence: UPGRADING-8.2.0.txt, '1. Backward Incompatible Changes' -> Standard: strtolower()/strtoupper() (and the related functions listed above) are no longer locale-sensitive and now perform ASCII-only case conversion as if the locale were "C"; mb_strtolower() remains available for locale-aware conversion. No PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 UPGRADING file revisits this behavior, so it persists unchanged through PHP 8.5.
